answer: The arbitrary-mass double-pole cut is a compact quadratic polynomial. Combining its three crossed logarithms with the exact PS tree amplitude gives a nonzero closed four-mass interference jet. It is singular in the collinear limit, so triangle and box sectors must participate before any comparison with the real -3/8 threshold coefficient.

bubble_log_interference_jet.numerator_basis: coefficient lists multiply s^(6-k)*t^k for k=0,...,6

collinear_expansion.interpretation: The bubble sector alone contains collinear logarithms enhanced by r^-2 and r^-1; it cannot be compared directly with the integrated real threshold.

double_pole_cut.construction: Start with internal masses y,z, integrate the ordinary two-body angular polynomial, include sqrt(Kallen(S,y,z))/S, then apply d_y d_z at y=z=0.
double_pole_cut.cut_normalization: d_y*d_z ordinary_cut = P/12 for physical S>0
